headline: Sabres place Jack Rathbone on waivers
take:
Per Daily Faceoff, the Sabres have placed Jack Rathbone on waivers. The outlet notes he has yet to suit up in an NHL or AHL game this season because of injury.

The move says little about Buffalo's strength, and the numbers explain why. The Sabres sit at 7-5-3 for 17 points through 15 games, and they've earned that record on an even footing. Their share of expected goals (a measure of chance quality) is 49.4 percent, and at five-on-five it's 50 percent, so they've been about level with opponents. They've scored four fewer goals than their chances would predict, and goals saved above expected for their goaltending is minus 0.9, a small negative. So far this season the special teams are quiet: the power play generates 0.64 expected goals per game, and the penalty kill allows 0.78 per game. Waiving a player who hasn't played doesn't change any of that, so we'd watch the finishing and goaltending numbers for Buffalo's direction, not this roster tweak.
